title: ARC output.yml
description: Mechanical definition of the consolidated output.yml contract ARC writes to <project_directory>/output/output.yml. Prose reference: docs/output_yml_schema.md. A key listed in 'required' is always emitted; a key whose type includes 'null' may be emitted as null; a key that is neither required nor null-typed is omitted entirely under the conditions stated in the reference. 'unevaluatedProperties'/'additionalProperties' are false wherever ARC controls the key set, so a field added to arc/output.py without a matching schema change fails validation.

schema_version.description: Output contract version. Emitted from arc.parser_evidence.OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VERSION, shared with the evidence sidecar's output_schema_version.

arkane_version.description: Version of the Arkane (RMG-Py) install ARC invoked for this run. It names the software that ran, not a claim about what it produced: Arkane prints this header when it starts, so a run that started and then failed is named here too, and 'atom_energy_corrections' and 'bond_additivity_corrections' may be empty while this field is populated. Read with 'arkane_git_commit' from one source: the header Arkane prints at the top of its own log under calcs/statmech/, and otherwise rmgpy/version.py under RMG_PATH. Null when neither source is readable. Prose reference: docs/output_yml_schema.md.

arkane_git_commit.description: RMG-Py (Arkane) repo HEAD commit hash, read from the same source as 'arkane_version'. Null when that source reports none, which is the normal case for a pip- or conda-installed RMG-Py.

rmg_database.description: Identity of the quantum corrections tables Arkane used: the quantum_corrections/data.py its own rmgpy settings point at (arkane.encorr.data.quantum_corrections_path, reported by the RMG conda environment), which is not necessarily the file under ARC's RMG_DB_PATH. 'quantum_corrections_sha256' is the SHA-256 of the bytes of that file. 'path_kind' is 'git' when the database root, three directories above that file, holds a .git (then 'git_commit' is its HEAD, read from the .git files), 'package' when it lies inside a conda prefix that lists the rmgdatabase package (then 'version' is that package's version), and 'unknown' otherwise. 'matches_arc_rmg_db_path' is whether the file ARC matches its correction keys against under RMG_DB_PATH has the same digest; on a mismatch a matched key may be missing or different in the file Arkane loaded. Each value that cannot be determined is null.

arc_aec_yml_sha256.description: SHA-256 of ARC's own data/AEC.yml, set only when ARC renders atomEnergies from it for the Arkane level of theory (arkane_level_of_theory), or for the composite or single-point level of the TS-check E0 run (Arkane then uses those atom energies). Null when it does not.

parser_evidence.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when the evidence sidecar could not be built or written.

cost_metrics.description: Run-level computational cost, aggregated from the per-job records the Scheduler collects. Prose reference: docs/output_yml_schema.md.

neb_level.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) unless the orca_neb TS adapter is among the adapters the scheduler uses (the user's ts_adapters, or ARC's defaults when none were given) and has a level.

scan_level.description: The requested level of the rotor scans: the level ARC's scan jobs are submitted at (before any troubleshooting or adaptive change). null when rotor scans were not requested (job_types.rotors false), and never a level for a scan that could not run. It is also null when an adaptive_levels entry names 'scan'.

irc_level.description: The requested level of the IRC jobs of the run's transition states. null when IRC was not requested (job_types.irc false) or the run has no transition state. A TS record's levels.irc is the level of the IRC jobs that actually produced its logs. It is also null when an adaptive_levels entry names 'irc'.

conformer_opt_level.description: The requested level of the conformer optimizations of non-TS species (the level of the conf_opt jobs, before any troubleshooting). null when no conformer optimization could run: conformer optimization was not requested (job_types.conf_opt false) and no conformer was optimized anyway, or the run has no non-monoatomic species that ARC computes (a species loaded from an Arkane yml file has no jobs). Each conformer's own level is that record's conformer_levels entry. It is also null when an adaptive_levels entry names 'conf_opt'.

conformer_sp_level.description: The requested level of the conformer single points that follow the conformer optimizations. null unless conformer single points were requested (job_types.conf_sp true), conformer optimization could run, and this level differs from the run's conformer optimization level (ARC skips a conformer single point at the level the conformer was optimized at). It is also null when an adaptive_levels entry names 'conf_sp'.

ts_guess_level.description: The requested level at which the guesses of a transition state are optimized and compared. null when the run has no transition state. It is used to optimize TS guesses as conformers when more than one guess succeeded, so a TS whose only successful guess is optimized directly has its opt level in levels.opt. It is also null when an adaptive_levels entry names 'conf_opt', the job type of the TS guess optimizations.

gsm_level.description: The level of the xtb_gsm path searches: {method: 'gfn2', software: 'xtb'}. It is stated only when the run has a GSM log and every archived per-node xtb output (gsm_node_outputs/*.xtbout) beside every GSM log shows the GFN2-xTB Hamiltonian and a program call with the charge and the number of unpaired electrons (multiplicity minus one) of the transition state record. null when the run has no GSM log, when a GSM log has no archived xtb output, or when an output shows another method, charge or spin.

adaptive_levels.description: The run's adaptive levels of theory, in the same structure ARC writes to restart.yml, with each level in the level_dict shape, or null when the run does not use adaptive_levels. Under adaptive levels each species' opt, freq and sp levels are chosen by its heavy-atom count (and a reaction's participants by the reaction-wide count), so the header opt_level, freq_level and sp_level are only run-level defaults and the level a species' logs were computed at is that record's 'levels'. Each entry gives a heavy-atom count range (the upper bound of the last range is the string 'inf') and a mapping from job types (space-joined when they share a level, e.g. 'opt freq') to the level.

freq_scale_factor_key.description: The entry key in ARC's data/freq_scale_factors.yml that 'freq_level' resolved to, e.g. "wb97xd/def2tzvp, software: gaussian". Null when the user supplied the factor, when the level has no entry in that file, or when the file cannot be read.

freq_scale_factor_source.description: The literature source the 'freq_scale_factor_key' entry points at, resolved through its explicit 'source' index against the top-level 'sources' mapping of the same file. Null whenever 'freq_scale_factor_key' is null, and also when the matched entry carries no resolvable index.

bac_type.description: Bond additivity correction type the run requested. Requested is not applied: ARC applies a BAC only in the thermo statmech run, so a rates-only run, every transition state, and a species whose own compute_thermo is off carry no bond_additivity record under energy_corrections regardless of this value.

atom_energy_corrections.description: Arkane's reference atomic electronic energies in hartree, keyed by element symbol.

bond_additivity_corrections.description: The Arkane BAC parameter table for the run's level of theory, in the model's native shape: a flat per-bond map in kcal/mol for Petersson, the nested per-element table for Melius.

wall_time_hrs.description: Wall-clock duration of the run in hours. Null when ARC has no recorded start time.

jobs_missing_time.description: Jobs recorded with no run time. They are excluded from both total_execution_time_hrs and total_core_hours.

jobs_missing_cores.description: Jobs that have a run time but no core count. They count toward total_execution_time_hrs but not total_core_hours.

per_ess.description: Per-ESS aggregates keyed by the job adapter name; records with no adapter are bucketed under 'unknown'. Null when no jobs were recorded.

petersson_bac_table.description: The Petersson BAC parameter table: per-bond parameters in kcal/mol, keyed by bond descriptor.

melius_bac_table.description: The Melius BAC parameter table in its native nested shape, as arkane.encorr.data.mbac stores it: three per-element parameter maps plus one scalar molecular correction.

level_dict.description: Level.as_dict() with the 'repr' and 'compatible_ess' keys removed. Only the level's non-None attributes appear, so the key set varies between runs.

solvation_scheme_level.description: Emitted by _level_to_dict as a nested level dict of the same shape.

args.description: Free-form ESS keyword blocks; the key set is the user's, not ARC's.

record_level_dict.description: A level_dict for a job that ran, as recorded in a species record. The 'software' key is absent: a level's software is only ARC's deduction of which program would run it. The program that ran an opt, freq, sp, composite or IRC job is stated by 'ess_software', and that of a rotor scan by the scan's own 'ess_software'; the programs of conformer jobs are not stated.

ess_versions.description: Full ESS version banners keyed by job type, parsed from each available log. Each value is the banner as the program printed it (e.g. 'Gaussian 16, Revision C.01'), not a bare version number. Pair each entry with the same job type in 'ess_software'. 'composite' is the composite-method log. 'irc' is present only when every IRC log of the record states the same banner. 'gsm' is the xtb banner of a transition state's archived GSM node outputs, present only when they all state the same one.

ess_software.description: The ESS that produced each available log, keyed by the same job types as 'ess_versions' and read from the same files, so a version banner can be paired with the program that produced it rather than with the software a level of theory declared. Values are ARC's lowercase ESS names ('gaussian', 'orca', 'molpro', ...). The key set is a superset of the 'ess_versions' key set. 'irc' is present only when every IRC log of the record was identified as the same program. 'gsm' is 'xtb', present only when every archived GSM node output of a transition state was identified as xtb.

constraint.description: One held-fixed coordinate parsed from an ESS input deck or log. index_base is the source convention: 1 for Gaussian, 0 for Orca. target_value is reported exactly as the source deck states it and is never converted; target_value_units names the unit it is in.

target_value_units.description: The unit of target_value, as the source deck states it and never converted. Angular constraints are degrees for every ESS. Length is 'angstrom' for both a Gaussian ModRedundant coordinate and an Orca '%geom Constraints' entry, which is the unit Orca reads by default and the one ARC writes; an Orca deck written elsewhere in Bohr carries a value this unit does not describe, because Orca does not echo the unit it was written in.

spin_diagnostic.description: S**2 spin contamination of the single-point wavefunction. null for restricted/closed-shell logs and for non-converged species.

log.description: Run-relative path of the ESS log the <S**2> value was read from. Null when that log lies outside the project directory and is therefore not part of the export.

correction_component.description: One native per-atom or per-bond term of an applied correction, as produced by arc/scripts/get_species_corrections.py.

parameter_unit.description: Pinned to hartree for an atom component and kcal_mol for a bond component by the 'allOf' branches below. Pinning it is what makes a silent kJ/mol-for-kcal/mol substitution a validation failure rather than a factor-of-4.184 error in a consumer.

energy_correction.description: One correction model ARC applied to this species, with its total, native decomposition, and the parameter table ARC used. A bond_additivity entry appears only where the thermo statmech run covered the species; the run-level bac_type records the request, this record the outcome.

model.description: The legal model names are enumerated once, per correction_type, in the 'allOf' branches below.

matched_arkane_key.description: The Arkane database key string ARC matched in the section this correction's parameters live in: the atom-energy section for an 'atom_energy' record, the Petersson or Melius bond-additivity section for a 'bond_additivity' one. The two are matched independently and may differ. Null when nothing matched in that section.

unit.description: Pinned to hartree for an atom-energy correction and kcal_mol for a bond-additivity one by the 'allOf' branches below.

skipped_components.description: The bonds of a Petersson bond-additivity correction that have no parameter in the matched table, as {bond, count}. Arkane's Petersson correction skips a bond type it has no parameter for and applies the rest, so 'components' lists the bonds that were applied and sums to 'total' (in kcal_mol), and this list names the bonds that contributed nothing. Empty when every bond has a parameter. Null where it does not apply: an atom-energy record and a Melius record.

reference_atom_energies.description: Atom-energy corrections only. Omitted (key absent, never null) when the run has no such table.

parameter_table.description: Petersson bond-additivity corrections only, and only when the key matched in the bond-additivity section is also the atom-energy key ARC hands Arkane as its model chemistry. Omitted (key absent, never null) otherwise.

scan_sample.description: One completed point of a 1D rotor scan.

angle_degrees.description: The ABSOLUTE value of the scanned dihedral at this point, in degrees, measured on this point's own geometry (coordinate.atom_indices, 1-based) rather than derived from the requested grid. It is not a displacement from the scan's first sample and nothing has to be added back to it. The sequence is unwrapped and never folded into a 0-360 window, so a full rotation ends a turn away from where it started (a scan from 59.867 ends at 419.867, which is the same angle modulo 360) and a scan that sweeps towards decreasing values goes below its start, possibly negative.

electronic_energy_hartree.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when the parser gave no aligned absolute-energy list.

geometry_xyz.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when the per-point geometries were unavailable or did not align 1:1 with the energies.

geometry_isotopes.description: The isotopes of geometry_xyz, taken only from a scan log that states the masses it used (a Gaussian log that printed 'Atom N has atomic number Z and mass M'); null for every other program and for a log that states none. Emitted together with geometry_xyz and omitted with it.

symmetry_number.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) unless ARC determined an integer symmetry of at least 1.

requested_step_size.description: The requested grid spacing in degrees, SIGNED: negative for a scan that sweeps towards decreasing dihedral values. Never 0. Omitted (key absent, never null) for ESS whose logs do not echo the requested grid.

requested_start.description: The requested starting dihedral in degrees. Grid metadata describing the extent that was asked for, NOT an anchor to add to a sample's angle_degrees. Omitted (key absent, never null) without a requested_step_size or a computable dihedral.

requested_end.description: requested_start + requested_step_size * steps, in degrees, and therefore below requested_start for a scan with a negative step size. Not wrapped: a full rotation lands a turn away from requested_start. Omitted (key absent, never null) under the same condition as requested_start.

zero_energy_reference_hartree.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when the parser reports none.

ess_software.description: The ESS that produced the scan log, identified from the log itself (ARC's lowercase ESS name). null when the log is missing or identifies no program.

ess_version.description: The full version banner the scan log states, as the program printed it. null when the log is missing or states none.

constraints.description: Held-fixed coordinates excluding the scanned coordinate. Omitted (key absent, never null) when none were found.

one_or_multi_dimensional_indices.description: An atom-index list taken straight from rotors_dict: a flat list of integers for a 1D rotor, or a list of such lists for an ND directed rotor, which the scheduler also marks successful.

treatment.description: The treatment Arkane applied to this rotor, read from its own output: 'hindered_rotor' or 'free_rotor'. Null when it is not known: the Arkane output was not parsed, Arkane kept a different number of rotors than ARC exported (it drops every rotor, and treats the species as a rigid rotor and harmonic oscillator, when the frequency log has no force-constant matrix), or Arkane used a multi-dimensional treatment. Never a default.

dimension.description: Rotor dimensionality. 1 for an ordinary 1D rotor; higher for an ND directed rotor, whose atom_indices and pivot_atoms are then lists of lists and whose barrier_kj_mol is null.

atom_indices.description: The rotor's 1-indexed scanned dihedral: a flat 4-atom list for a 1D rotor, one such list per dimension for an ND directed rotor.

pivot_atoms.description: The rotor's 1-indexed rotation axis, dimensioned exactly as atom_indices.

rejected_torsion.description: A rotor ARC evaluated and genuinely rejected (rotors_dict entry whose 'success' is False), carried so a consumer can tell 'no rotors' from 'rotors found and rejected, for these reasons' rather than losing the rejected rotor entirely. Pending or never-attempted rotors ('success' is None) are not carried here -- ARC has not decided their fate yet. This rotor never contributes a rotor_scans record -- rejected rotors are excluded from rotor_scans entirely -- so source_log records the raw scan-log path directly rather than referencing a rotor_scans key.

rotor_index.description: The rotor's key in rotors_dict, i.e. its identifying index among the species' rotors (not an atom index).

invalidation_reason.description: ARC's recorded reason(s) the rotor was rejected, verbatim. An empty string means ARC recorded no specific reason -- not that one was fabricated here. This is accumulated with '+=' across troubleshooting rounds, so it may contain more than one concatenated reason rather than a single discrete one.

atom_indices.description: The rotor's 1-indexed scanned dihedral, when recorded: a flat 4-atom list for a 1D rotor, one such list per dimension for an ND directed rotor. Null when rotors_dict has no 'scan' entry for this rotor.

pivot_atoms.description: The rotor's 1-indexed rotation axis, when recorded, dimensioned exactly as atom_indices. Null when rotors_dict has no 'pivots' entry for this rotor.

dimension.description: Rotor dimensionality, exactly as the successful torsion shape's 'dimension'. 1 for an ordinary 1D rotor; higher for an ND directed rotor, whose atom_indices and pivot_atoms are then lists of lists.

source_log.description: The rejected rotor's scan log path, relative to the project directory (bare os.path.relpath, no containment check -- a log outside the project directory yields a '../..'-prefixed path; same behavior as rotor_scans[].source_log, not changed here), when one is found on disk at write time. Omitted entirely (never null) when rotors_dict records no on-disk scan for this rotor. IMPORTANT: this field's absence does NOT mean the rotor was never a torsion -- it only means no scan log was found on disk when output.yml was written. A genuinely-scanned rotor can still lack this field: a restart-restored rejected rotor's stale relative scan_path is only repaired for rotors where success is truthy, so it routinely fails the on-disk check; a failed directed scan has its scan_path deliberately blanked to '' while still recording a real invalidation_reason; and a TS reaction-zone pivot exclusion sets success=False for policy reasons, typically before any scan is attempted. ARC's rotors_dict does not currently distinguish these rejection stages from a genuine 'not a torsion' determination -- invalidation_reason is the only (free-text, imperfect) signal available. Deliberately not a rotor_scans[].key reference: rejected rotors never produce a rotor_scans record (rotor_scans only admits success=True rotors), and a rejected rotor's log may itself be truncated or self-inconsistent, so this records where the evidence is rather than a parsed result.

e0_kj_mol.description: Arkane's E0 (electronic energy plus scaled ZPE) in kJ/mol. With atom corrections on (see e0_atom_corrections_applied) Arkane adds atom_hf - atom_thermal per atom, so it is the 0 K enthalpy of formation minus the sum of n_i * atom_thermal_i, not the 0 K formation enthalpy itself; a TS's E0 is never a formation enthalpy.

e0_atom_corrections_applied.description: Whether the Arkane run that wrote e0_kj_mol had its atom energy correction switched on. When false, e0_kj_mol is an absolute electronic energy plus ZPE. Null when the run's switches are not known, and for a species loaded from an Arkane YAML.

e0_bond_corrections_applied.description: Whether the Arkane run that wrote e0_kj_mol had its bond additivity correction switched on. The thermo and E0-only runs use the run's bac_type; the kinetics run and the TS-check E0 run use none. Null when not known.

arkane_rotors_applied.description: The number of rotor modes (HinderedRotor, FreeRotor, HinderedRotor2D, HinderedRotorClassicalND, and Mode, which is how Arkane writes a multi-dimensional rotor) in the conformer block of the output.py of the last Arkane run that wrote this species' conformer block. It counts modes, not torsional degrees of freedom. 0 when Arkane dropped every rotor; it can be lower than the number of torsions. Null when that output was not parsed.

arkane_treatment.description: The statmech treatment Arkane applied, derived from the rotor modes of that block: 'rrho' with no rotor mode, 'rrho_1d' when every rotor mode is a HinderedRotor or FreeRotor, 'rrho_nd' when every one is a HinderedRotor2D or HinderedRotorClassicalND, 'rrho_1d_nd' when both kinds are present. Null when the output was not parsed, and when any rotor mode is of unknown kind (a Mode entry).

rigid_rotor_kind.description: The rigid-rotor kind from the principal moments of inertia of the exported final geometry: 'linear' for a linear species, 'spherical_top' when all three moments agree and 'symmetric_top' when two do (each within a relative tolerance of 1e-3), and 'asymmetric_top' otherwise. When every atom carries its most common isotope the exported point_group refines this: a group with no C_n (n >= 3) and no S4 axis that is not cubic rules out a symmetric or spherical top, and a group with such an axis promotes a geometry whose moments agree within 1e-2. Null when there is no final geometry, when it cannot be weighed, and when the species is flagged non-linear but its atoms are collinear. 'atom' is never written here: statmech is null for monoatomic species. It is a geometric label only: Arkane treats every non-linear species as a NonlinearRotor.

thermo_point.description: One tabulated temperature. Only temperature_k is guaranteed: the Tdata/Cpdata fallback in _thermo_to_dict emits Cp alone, while arc/scripts/save_arkane_thermo.py emits all five.

standard_state_pressure_pa.description: Standard-state pressure in Pa that s298_j_mol_k, the NASA polynomials and every thermo_points entropy and free energy belong to. It is 101325 (1 atm) for every thermo ARC takes from an Arkane run: Arkane's translational partition function divides by the literal 101325. (rmgpy/statmech/translation.pyx), and nothing configures it. When the Arkane run's thermo.yaml carries the value, arc/scripts/save_arkane_thermo.py recovered it from that partition function; when the thermo.yaml is missing or carries none, ARC reads the thermo from the run's output.py and records the same constant. null for a thermo that did not come from an Arkane run ARC invoked, which no ARC path produces.

atom_corrections_applied.description: Whether the Arkane run that produced this thermo had its atom energy correction switch (useAtomCorrections) on. false means Arkane subtracted no atom energies, so h298_kj_mol, the NASA polynomials and every thermo_points enthalpy and free energy are absolute electronic-structure energies. true means only that the switch was on: the atom energies subtracted are those of atom_corrections_level, which need not be the level the species' energies were computed at, so compare the two before treating the enthalpies as formation enthalpies. null when the thermo did not come from an Arkane run that recorded it, including a species Arkane loaded from its own YAML file.

bond_corrections_applied.description: The useBondCorrections value of the Arkane run that produced this thermo. ARC disables bond additivity corrections whenever it disables atom energy corrections. true does not mean every bond had a parameter: Arkane skips a bond type its Petersson table lacks. null exactly when atom_corrections_applied is null.

atom_corrections_level.description: The level whose atom energies Arkane subtracted (the level ARC matched Arkane's model chemistry for, or whose data/AEC.yml entry it passed as atomEnergies), in the same shape as sp_level and composite_method so it can be compared with the level of the species' energies. A level that differs from that energy level means h298_kj_mol mixes two levels and is not a formation enthalpy. null unless atom_corrections_applied is true. The comparison is on method (with dispersion folded in, whether the level carries it in the method string or a separate dispersion field) and basis, normalized as in ARC's Arkane database matching (case, hyphens and spaces ignored, a trailing four-digit refit year stripped from the method). ARC's Arkane matching folds the dispersion in the same way, so the atom energies applied carry this level's dispersion correction. Arkane has no corrections for solvated levels, so this is never a level with a solvation_method: when the energy level has one and this field is not null, gas-phase atom energies were subtracted from solvated energies, and the enthalpies should not be treated as formation enthalpies. Under adaptive_levels each species' energy level differs from the header sp_level: compare with the record's levels.composite, else levels.sp. When not null the value repeats arkane_level_of_theory; its information is where it is null.

ts_guess.description: Sanitized attribution for the chosen TS guess. The list is empty when no guess was chosen.

common_species_fields.description: The fields every species and transition-state record carries.

xyz_isotopes.description: The isotope mass number of each atom of xyz, in the atom order of xyz: the isotopes on ARC's species geometry; ARC does not write isotopes into ESS input decks, so this list says nothing about the masses an ESS used. Null when ARC holds no isotope list for the geometry, including the synthesized one-atom geometry of a monoatomic species.

conformers.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when ARC screened no conformers.

conformer_energies.description: One ABSOLUTE energy per screened conformer, not relative to the lowest. Emitted and omitted together with 'conformers', which 'dependentRequired' enforces. The two lists are index-aligned, a relation JSON Schema cannot express; arc/output_schema_test.py asserts it against the producer instead. An entry is null for a conformer that has no energy: upload no energy for it. conformer_energy_kind, conformer_energy_level and conformer_force_field describe only the entries that are not null. The unit of an entry depends on where it came from: kcal/mol for a force-field energy of the conformer screen, kJ/mol for an electronic energy parsed from a conformer optimization or conformer single-point log. A conformer whose optimization failed keeps its force-field geometry and its force-field energy, so one list can mix the two units. conformer_energy_kind states the unit of the entries that are not null, and is null when they mix them.

conformer_levels.description: The level of the conformer optimization job that produced each geometry of 'conformers', index-aligned with it (always the same length). An entry is null for a geometry that was never optimized (a force-field geometry, including the geometry kept by a conformer whose optimization failed, or a user-supplied one) and for a geometry whose level was not recorded (a restart written before this key existed). Captured from the job that produced the geometry, so it includes conformer troubleshooting at another level. The level of a conformer single point is not recorded here, since it does not change the geometry: see conformer_energy_level. null when the record has no conformers, which includes every transition state (TS guesses are not exported as conformers).

conformer_energy_kind.description: The unit and origin of conformer_energies: 'force_field_kcal_mol' when every energy held is a force-field energy known to be in kcal/mol for the force field and backend that computed it, 'electronic_kj_mol' when every energy held is an electronic energy in kJ/mol parsed from an ESS log (conformer optimization, or conformer single point when it ran). null when there are no conformers or no energy in the list, when the list mixes the two kinds (some conformers optimized, others, e.g. after a failed optimization, still holding force-field energies), when the origin of an energy was not recorded (a restart written before this key existed, or energies read from a user-supplied conformers file), when an energy is a placeholder no force field computed (a cheat-sheet, monoatomic or diatomic species), and when the force field's energy unit is not known to be kcal/mol (e.g. UFF or Ghemical energies from OpenBabel, which are kJ/mol).

conformer_energy_level.description: The level the electronic energies of conformer_energies were computed at: the conformer single-point level when conformer single points overwrote the optimization energies, else the conformer optimization level. null unless conformer_energy_kind is 'electronic_kj_mol' and every energy held was computed at one and the same level; null for force-field energies (they have no level) and when the energies came from different levels (e.g. only some conformers got a single point).

conformer_force_field.description: The force field and backend that produced conformer_energies, e.g. 'MMFF94s (rdkit)' or 'UFF (rdkit)' (RDKit falls back from MMFF to UFF when MMFF cannot be set up). Set when every energy held was produced by one and the same force field and backend, including one whose energy unit is not known to be kcal/mol (then conformer_energy_kind is null); null when there are no conformers or no energy, for electronic energies, for placeholder energies no force field computed, when energies came from different force fields or backends, and when the force field was not recorded (a restart written before this key existed).

coarse_opt_input_xyz_isotopes.description: The isotopes of coarse_opt_input_xyz, which is ARC's species initial geometry: the isotopes on ARC's species geometry; ARC does not write isotopes into ESS input decks, so this list says nothing about the masses an ESS used. Null exactly when coarse_opt_input_xyz is null or ARC holds no isotope list for it.

coarse_opt_output_xyz_isotopes.description: The isotopes of coarse_opt_output_xyz, which is parsed from the coarse opt log, taken only from a log that states the masses it used (a Gaussian log that printed 'Atom N has atomic number Z and mass M'). Null for every other program, for a log that states none (an opt-only Gaussian log does not), and when coarse_opt_output_xyz is null.

opt_input_xyz_isotopes.description: The isotopes of opt_input_xyz. When a coarse stage ran this is coarse_opt_output_xyz_isotopes (stated by the coarse log, else null); otherwise opt_input_xyz is ARC's species initial geometry and these are the isotopes on ARC's species geometry; ARC does not write isotopes into ESS input decks, so this list says nothing about the masses an ESS used. Null when opt_input_xyz is null or no list is available.

composite_log.description: The log of the composite-method job (CBS-QB3, G4, ...) that produced the geometry and energy of a composite run, relative to the project directory. null for a run that is not a composite run.

opt_route.description: The effective keyword line the opt job ran with, read from the log's echoed route and, only when the log holds none, from the input deck beside it. The program is the one the log itself states. Gaussian: the first route section of the file (a --Link1-- file reports its first job only), with a log's wrapped lines rejoined and a deck's lines joined by single spaces. Orca: the lowercase '!' keyword lines only, without their '!' and any '#' comment, joined by single spaces; '%' blocks are not included. Observed, never rebuilt from a level of theory: null for any other program, for an unconverged species, and when no keyword line is found. When the sp result was taken from the opt log, sp_route is this line too.

freq_route.description: As opt_route, for the freq job and freq_log.

sp_route.description: As opt_route, for the sp job and sp_log.

composite_route.description: As opt_route, for the composite-method job and composite_log.

sp_t1_diagnostic.description: The T1 diagnostic (unitless) ARC's parser read from the sp log. It is stated only when the recorded sp level (levels.sp) is a coupled-cluster method (its name contains 'cc') or qcisd; null for every other level, for an unconverged species, and when the log prints none.

opt_dipole_moment_debye.description: The total dipole moment in Debye of the last 'Dipole moment (field-independent basis, Debye)' block of a Gaussian opt log, at the final geometry of the opt job. Null for any other program, for an unconverged species, for a charged species (the dipole of an ion depends on the origin), for a monoatomic species, and when the log prints no block.

opt_dipole_moment_density.description: The density the dipole moment of opt_dipole_moment_debye was computed from, as the word of the Gaussian header 'Population analysis using the <X> density' that precedes that block (for example 'SCF' or 'current'). Null exactly when the header is absent or opt_dipole_moment_debye is null.

freq_polarizability_angstrom3.description: The isotropic static polarizability in angstrom^3 at the freq level: a third of the trace of the last 'Exact polarizability' line (atomic units, bohr^3) of a Gaussian freq log, converted with ARC's bohr_to_angstrom. Null for any other program, for an unconverged species, when the log prints no such line, and for a monoatomic species (no freq job is run, so it is not computed).

composite_input.description: The input deck of the composite-method job, a sibling of composite_log, when it is on disk. null otherwise.

freq_hessian_method.description: How the frequency job's Hessian was built, in TCKDB's HessianMethod vocabulary: the provenance of the method ARC requested, resolved through the documented behaviour of the ESS that ran it (a Gaussian Freq=Numer/EnOnly route, the method class under a bare Gaussian freq, an Orca NumFreq/NumGrad/AnFreq keyword line, the PySCF adapter's multiplicity branch). Null wherever the request does not settle the answer, including every other ESS, a composite level, an unlisted method, and a species with no converged frequency job. Prose reference: docs/output_yml_schema.md.

freq_final_settings.description: Always null: ARC has no reliable signal for freq jobs yet.

sp_final_settings.description: Always null: ARC has no reliable signal for sp jobs yet.

levels.description: The level of theory (requested, not observed) of the job whose log this record exports under each job key: the 'levels' of the job that wrote opt_log ('opt'), freq_log ('freq'), sp_log ('sp'), the composite job's log ('composite'), and, for a TS, the IRC logs ('irc'). Captured from the job when the scheduler recorded its log path, so it is the level that job ran at under adaptive levels, reaction-wide overrides and troubleshooting, and not the run-level opt_level, freq_level or sp_level. For a composite method 'sp' repeats 'composite' and 'freq' is null, since the composite log's frequencies are at a level the composite level does not name (a freq_log that is the composite log pairs with 'composite'). A monoatomic species has no opt job, so its 'opt' is null. Every key is always present; a value is null where no such job ran, where the level was not recorded (an older run or a restart written before levels were recorded), and, for 'irc', on every record that is not a TS or whose forward and reverse IRC jobs ran at different levels. A level here states no 'software'. 'ess_software' states the program of the opt, freq and sp logs only; the programs of composite, IRC and conformer jobs are not stated. When the single point is not requested, sp_energy_hartree is read from the optimization log and pairs with 'opt', and 'sp' is null.

conformers_isotopes.description: Index-aligned with conformers: the isotopes of each conformer on ARC's species geometry (ARC does not write isotopes into ESS input decks). An entry is null for a conformer ARC holds only as text. Emitted and omitted together with 'conformers'.

conformer_ess_software.description: Index-aligned with conformers: the ESS that ran the conformer optimization that produced each conformer geometry, identified from that optimization log as for ess_software. A conformer single point does not change it: the single point's geometry, which the scheduler may write into conformers, is not what this names. An entry is null for a conformer whose geometry came from no ESS optimization (a force-field geometry, a conformer whose optimization failed, or a user-supplied one), whose log was not recorded (a restart written before this key existed), or whose log is missing or states no program. Emitted and omitted together with 'conformers' and conformer_ess_version.

conformer_ess_version.description: Index-aligned with conformers: the full version banner the program printed in the conformer optimization log named by the matching conformer_ess_software entry, as for ess_versions. An entry is null whenever that entry is null, and when the log states no banner. Emitted and omitted together with 'conformers' and conformer_ess_software.

species_record.description: A non-TS species. The TS-only fields must be absent, which 'unevaluatedProperties: false' enforces.

irc_endpoint_of.description: The label of the TS whose IRC produced this species, for an IRC endpoint species (labeled IRC_<ts label>_<n>, optimized from an end of the IRC path), and null for every ordinary species. An endpoint is not a stable well ARC was asked about but the geometry the IRC reached, so a consumer that treats species records as wells should skip a record where this is not null. The TS's own record lists no endpoints; this key exists on species records only.

irc_endpoint_direction.description: The direction of the IRC job whose log produced this endpoint, 'forward' or 'reverse'. Null for an ordinary species, and null for an endpoint whose direction was not recorded. The <n> in the label is the order in which the IRC jobs finished and says nothing about direction. It is the sign of the IRC job's transition vector in the ESS and carries no reactant or product meaning.

ts_record.description: A transition state: every species field plus the TS-only fields.

irc_log_routes.description: Index-aligned with irc_logs: the effective keyword line of each IRC job, as for opt_route (the log's echoed route first). null for a log that is missing, from another program, or that holds no keyword line.

irc_log_directions.description: Index-aligned with irc_logs: which branch of the reaction path each log traversed. null when ARC did not record a direction for that log. Getting this wrong swaps reactant and product silently, so the value is constrained rather than free text.

irc_log_levels.description: Index-aligned with irc_logs: the level of the IRC job that produced each log (job.level, without a software, since ess_software.irc is the observed program). null for a log whose job level was not recorded (an older run or restart). Unlike levels.irc, which is null when the two logs differ, this keeps each log's own level.

freq_frequencies_cm1_ess_order.description: Every vibrational frequency (cm-1) of the frequency job, as printed by the ESS (ascending for Gaussian, ORCA and Q-Chem), with the imaginary modes (negative numbers) in place. Unlike imaginary_frequencies_cm1, which is re-sorted most-negative first, and statmech.harmonic_frequencies_cm1, which drops the imaginary modes, this list keeps each mode's position. Null when the frequencies were not recorded and for a TS that did not converge.

reaction_coordinate_mode_index.description: The 1-based index, into freq_frequencies_cm1_ess_order, of the mode the normal mode displacement check validated as the reaction coordinate: the most negative frequency. Null unless ts_checks.NMD is true and the check genuinely passed (a failed check that skip_nmd forced to pass leaves it null), and null unless exactly one entry of freq_frequencies_cm1_ess_order equals, within 0.01 cm-1, the frequency of the mode the check analysed.

nmd_forced.description: Whether ts_checks.NMD was forced to true after the normal mode displacement check failed (the skip_nmd option), as the check's own record states. true: the check failed and ARC forced the verdict to a pass. false: the check ran and ARC did not force it, whatever its verdict. null when no check record exists (the check did not run, or the record was not saved by an older run), including when ts_checks.NMD is not a boolean.

irc_converged.description: Whether the IRC JOBS COMPLETED, not whether the IRC validated the transition state. It is true once both IRC job directions finished, whatever their endpoints turned out to be, and null when the run did not request IRC at all. The validation verdict is ts_checks.IRC.

irc_participant_mapping.description: Which atoms of each optimized IRC endpoint geometry belong to which participant species, recorded only when the IRC check established its verdict by graph isomorphism of the perceived endpoint fragments (graph isomorphism ignores stereochemistry, so stereoisomers with isomorphic graphs, such as E/Z isomers, may have their labels swapped; membership is the distance-threshold connectivity of the optimized endpoint geometry). Null when only the bond-list fallback decided, when IRC was not run or did not validate the TS (ts_checks.IRC is not true), and when it was not recorded. Atom indices are 0-based and count into the optimized geometry of the endpoint species; they are TS atom indices only when atom_order_matches_ts is true. Only atom-set membership is recorded, not the atom-to-atom correspondence within a participant. Which endpoint fragment is which occurrence of a repeated species is arbitrary, and occurrence k is independent of the k-th block of the reaction's atom_map.

sides_distinguishable.description: False when the reactants and the products are graph-isomorphic to each other (for example CH3 + CH4 to CH4 + CH3, or a degenerate rearrangement), in which case which endpoint is called the reactants is a convention.

atom_order_matches_ts.description: True when both IRC endpoint geometries have the element sequence of the TS geometry the IRC was run from, which states that atom i of an endpoint is atom i of the TS (ARC's IRC and optimization jobs keep the input atom order; the check cannot detect a swap of two atoms of the same element). False when the element sequences differ. Null when there was no TS geometry to compare to.

ts_checks.description: ARC's own verdicts on the transition state, one per validation it runs. true is a pass, false a failure, and null 'not run or no conclusion reached' - null is NOT a failure. These are the provenance of the transition state: irc_converged reports only that the IRC jobs completed, and only ts_checks.IRC says whether the IRC endpoints matched the reaction.

E0.description: The zero-point-corrected energy of the transition state lies above both reaction wells.

e_elect.description: The electronic energy of the transition state lies above both reaction wells.

IRC.description: The intrinsic reaction coordinate connects this transition state to the reaction's own reactants and products.

freq.description: The frequency calculation yielded exactly one imaginary mode, of a magnitude consistent with the reaction.

NMD.description: The imaginary mode's normal mode displacement moves the atoms whose bonds the reaction forms and breaks.

warnings.description: Free text accumulated by the checks above. An empty string means no check raised anything.

endpoint.description: Whether the geometry is the first (1) or the second (2) IRC endpoint geometry the IRC check compared.

endpoint_label.description: The label of the IRC endpoint species whose optimized geometry the atom indices count into. Null when the check was not told the label.

position.description: 1-based position of the participant in the order of the reaction's atom_map_reactant_labels (or atom_map_product_labels), which is not the order of reactant_labels.

occurrence.description: 1-based count of this label among the participants up to and including this one.

atom_indices.description: Ascending 0-based atom indices into the optimized IRC endpoint geometry.

kinetics.description: Fitted modified-Arrhenius kinetics. Every key is emitted; a value is null when the source dict did not carry it.

A_units.description: The unit string Arkane fitted A in, verbatim. It cannot be pinned by this schema because it depends on the reaction's molecularity ('s^-1' for unimolecular, 'cm^3/(mol*s)' or 'm^3/(mol*s)' for bimolecular, and so on). A consumer must read it rather than assume one.

Ea_units.description: The unit string Arkane fitted Ea in, verbatim ('kJ/mol' or 'kcal/mol'). Not pinned for the same reason as A_units: ARC reports the source's own unit rather than converting.

T0_k.description: The reference temperature in K of k = A (T/T0)^n exp(-Ea/RT). A and n cannot be interpreted without it.

dA.description: MULTIPLICATIVE uncertainty factor on A, dimensionless, as Arkane reports it ('dA = *|/ 1.48466'). The one-sigma band is [A / dA, A * dA] - NOT A +/- dA. dn and dEa beside it are additive, which is why this field carries no units sibling: there is no unit to carry.

dn.description: ADDITIVE uncertainty on n: the band is n +/- dn. Dimensionless.

dEa.description: ADDITIVE uncertainty on Ea: the band is Ea +/- dEa, in dEa_units.

atom_corrections_applied.description: Whether the Arkane kinetics run that fitted these parameters had its atom energy correction switched on, which decides what the TS's statmech.e0_kj_mol is. Null when the kinetics did not come from that run.

comment.description: The comment Arkane attached to the fitted Arrhenius expression, verbatim, plus, for a rate whose TS failed the IRC check, the ts_validation marker on a further line. Null when the kinetics carry none (user-supplied or restored kinetics).

ts_validation.description: A human-readable summary ARC stamps when it computed this rate from a TS that positively failed its IRC check (ts_checks.IRC is false); a consumer should read the TS record's ts_checks for the structured verdict. Null when ARC found no such failure, which includes an IRC check that was not performed.

reactant_labels.description: The labels of the reaction's reactant species, sorted and de-duplicated: an A + A reaction lists A once. It is not the stoichiometry; reactant_species_labels is.

product_labels.description: The labels of the reaction's product species, sorted and de-duplicated: an A + A reaction lists A once. It is not the stoichiometry; product_species_labels is.

reactant_species_labels.description: The reactant species with one entry per occurrence, in the order of ARCReaction.get_reactants_and_products, so HO2 + HO2 <=> H2O2 + O2 lists HO2 twice. When atom_map is not null this list equals atom_map_reactant_labels. Always an array for a reaction ARC ran.

product_species_labels.description: The product species with one entry per occurrence, in the order of ARCReaction.get_reactants_and_products. When atom_map is not null this list equals atom_map_product_labels. Always an array for a reaction ARC ran.

atom_map.description: ARC's reactant-to-product atom map, as the reaction holds it; it is never computed at export, so it is null when ARC had not mapped the reaction, and it is also null unless the map is a permutation that conserves the element (reactant atom i and product atom atom_map[i] have the same element). Entry i is the 0-based index of the product atom that reactant atom i becomes. Reactant atoms are counted over atom_map_reactant_labels in that order, each occurrence contributing the atoms of that species in the atom order of its exported geometry, one block per occurrence (so CH3 + CH3 has two blocks of four); product atoms are counted the same way over atom_map_product_labels. The order is that of the reaction's species lists, not that of reactant_labels, which is sorted and de-duplicated. Among symmetry-equivalent atoms (which hydrogen of CH4, which CH3 block) the choice is arbitrary and not specific to the reactive site. It says nothing about the atom order of the transition state; ts_atom_map states the TS atom of every atom.

atom_map_reactant_labels.description: The label of each of the reactants in the order atom_map counts their atoms, one entry per occurrence (a species that occurs twice is listed twice). Null exactly when atom_map is null.

atom_map_product_labels.description: The label of each of the products in the order atom_map counts their atoms, one entry per occurrence (a species that occurs twice is listed twice). Null exactly when atom_map is null.

atom_map_source.description: Where atom_map came from: 'inferred' when ARC computed it with its own mapping algorithm (a restart preserves this), 'declared' when it was explicitly declared as a user-given map. Null when atom_map is null and when its origin was not recorded (an input or restart dict that states no source, or an unknown value).

long_kinetic_description.description: Omitted (key absent, never null) when the reaction carries no description.

atom_map_method.description: The algorithm that computed an inferred atom_map (ARC's mapping driver, with the reaction family when known). Null unless atom_map_source is 'inferred'.

reversible.description: Whether the reaction is written as reversible: true for the '<=>' arrow, false for '=>'. ARC writes every reaction with '<=>', so every reaction ARC exports is true; false is not produced. Null when the arrow is unknown. It states the notation of the label, not a measured or computed reversibility.

ts_atom_map.description: The 0-based atom of the transition state that every atom of the reaction is, from a label-preserving isomorphism of two condensed graphs of reaction (CGRs): the reactant-indexed CGR (the concatenated reactant atoms, bonds that are in the reactants or in the products, from atom_map) and the TS-indexed CGR (the TS atoms, bonds of the two IRC endpoint geometries). That endpoint atom i is TS atom i is inferred from the endpoint geometries having the element sequence of the TS. Before the CGRs are compared, the bond graph of each endpoint must be isomorphic to that of its side, and the map is kept only if, on the TS geometry, every bond of both the reactants and the products is at a bonded distance and every bond that forms or breaks is at most a partial-bond distance. It is a constitutional (2D) correspondence: symmetry-equivalent atoms, diastereotopic ones included, are assigned by a deterministic convention. 'reactants' has one entry per concatenated reactant atom, in the order of atom_map_reactant_labels (each occurrence contributing the atoms of its species in the atom order of its exported geometry), and 'products' one per concatenated product atom, in the order of atom_map_product_labels, so products[atom_map[i]] == reactants[i]. 'reactant_endpoint' is the IRC endpoint (1 or 2, in the order the IRC check received them) whose bonds served as the reactants. 'ts_atom_order_follows_reactants' is true exactly when reactants is the identity. Null, with ts_atom_map_unavailable_reason, whenever it cannot be stated; atom_map itself is never altered by it.

ts_atom_map_unavailable_reason.description: Why ts_atom_map is null: no_ts (the reaction has no TS, or the TS has no geometry), irc_not_passed (ts_checks.IRC is not true), irc_fallback_path (the IRC verdict came from the bond-list fallback, which has no atom correspondence), atom_order_mismatch (the IRC endpoint geometries do not have the element sequence of the TS), no_atom_map (the reaction exports no atom_map), endpoint_perception_mismatch (the bonds perceived on an endpoint geometry are not the bond graph of its side), atom_map_contradicts_ts (the bonds the endpoints form and break are not those of atom_map, so no isomorphism exists), ts_geometry_contradicts_map (an isomorphism exists, but a bond it maps is at an implausible distance in the TS geometry), species_atom_order_mismatch (the geometry of a reactant or product does not have the atom order of the molecule the atom map counts in), computation_failed (the computation raised an error, which is logged), not_recorded (an older restart, or a malformed record that was dropped). Null exactly when ts_atom_map is not null.

negative_eigenvector.description: A negative root of the wavefunction stability matrix.

label.description: The ESS's label for the perturbation the root came from.

wavefunction_stability.description: Verdict of a wavefunction stability analysis. null when no analysis was run, its log is missing, or the log holds no verdict.

n_analyses.description: Number of stability analyses the log holds (ORCA).

followed_to_stable.description: Whether the ESS relaxed the instability into a stable solution (ORCA).

measured_on_ts_guess.description: Index of the abandoned TS guess a carried-over verdict was measured on.

log.description: Run-relative path of the stability analysis log.

scf_reference.description: Which source decided the species' open-shell character, and the SCF references the sp and freq jobs actually ran with.
